signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: What is the first split when assessing genital discharge?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: By sex and site: male urethral discharge (urethritis) versus female vaginal/cervical discharge. This immediately narrows the likely causes and the swabs needed.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: How does the character of male urethral discharge help distinguish gonorrhoea from non-gonococcal urethritis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Profuse, purulent discharge with dysuria suggests gonorrhoea; scant, mucoid discharge suggests non-gonococcal urethritis (usually chlamydia or Mycoplasma genitalium). Both need NAAT confirmation.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: A woman has thick, white, 'cottage-cheese' discharge with vulval itch and no offensive odour. Diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. It is not sexually transmitted and is commoner in diabetes, pregnancy and after antibiotics; diagnosis is largely clinical.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: A woman has a thin, grey, homogeneous discharge with a fishy odour and little itch. Diagnosis and key tests?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Bacterial vaginosis — anaerobic overgrowth with loss of lactobacilli. Vaginal pH is >4.5 and microscopy shows clue cells (Amsel criteria). It is not an STI but is linked to preterm birth in pregnancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: A woman has a frothy, yellow-green, offensive discharge with itch and a 'strawberry cervix'. Diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis) — a sexually transmitted protozoan. Confirm with NAAT or wet-mount (motile trichomonads) and perform a full STI screen with partner notification.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: What features indicate pelvic inflammatory disease, and how is it managed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Deep pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, fever, mucopurulent cervix and cervical motion tenderness. Treat empirically with antibiotics without waiting for swabs, as delay risks tubal damage, infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: Why must gonorrhoea always be cultured, not just tested by NAAT?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Because Neisseria gonorrhoeae is increasingly antibiotic-resistant; culture provides antimicrobial sensitivities to guide and monitor treatment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: What is cervicitis and what are its typical features?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Inflammation of the cervix, usually from chlamydia or gonorrhoea, presenting with a mucopurulent cervical discharge and post-coital or inter-menstrual bleeding.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: Which investigations constitute the minimum work-up for genital discharge?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: NAAT for chlamydia and gonorrhoea (first-pass urine in men, vulvovaginal swab in women), gonococcal culture, vaginal pH and microscopy where relevant, and a full STI screen (HIV, syphilis) with a pregnancy test.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: What are the standard first-line treatments for gonorrhoea, chlamydia/NGU, BV/trichomonas, and candida?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Gonorrhoea: ceftriaxone. Chlamydia/NGU: doxycycline. Bacterial vaginosis and trichomonas: metronidazole. Candida: a topical or oral antifungal (e.g. clotrimazole or fluconazole).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: Why is partner notification essential in sexually transmitted causes of discharge?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: To treat asymptomatic partners, prevent reinfection of the index patient, and interrupt onward transmission; it is a core part of managing any STI.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.front: A neonate develops a purulent conjunctivitis in the first weeks of life. What must be considered and why?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.back: Ophthalmia neonatorum from maternal gonococcal or chlamydial infection acquired at delivery. It needs urgent treatment as gonococcal infection can threaten sight.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is the single most useful discriminator when assessing a genital ulcer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Painful versus painless (and single versus multiple). Painful, multiple, vesicle-preceded ulcers suggest herpes; a painless, solitary, indurated ulcer suggests primary syphilis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Describe the typical ulcer of genital herpes.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Painful, multiple, shallow ulcers preceded by vesicles on an erythematous base, with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy; the first episode may be severe with dysuria and systemic upset. Diagnose with HSV PCR of the lesion.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Describe the primary syphilitic chancre and why it matters.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A painless, solitary, indurated ulcer with a clean base and non-tender rubbery nodes. It is highly infectious and, if untreated, progresses to secondary and tertiary syphilis; in pregnancy it risks congenital syphilis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: How is syphilis confirmed at the ulcer stage?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Dark-ground microscopy of the lesion (for spirochaetes) and treponemal serology. Treatment is with benzathine penicillin, plus partner notification and screening.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What are the features of chancroid?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A painful, ragged, undermined ulcer caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, with suppurative (fluctuant) inguinal buboes. It is uncommon in the UK and considered with relevant travel/exposure.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) and its classic sign?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: An STI caused by specific chlamydia serovars: a small, often painless initial ulcer followed by large inguinal buboes; the 'groove sign' (nodes above and below the inguinal ligament) is characteristic.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Which non-infective condition causes recurrent oral AND genital ulcers, and what else may accompany it?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Behcet's disease. It also features uveitis, skin lesions and a positive pathergy test, and is managed with rheumatology input.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What ulcer features should raise suspicion of penile or vulval carcinoma?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A chronic, indurated, non-healing ulcer with a rolled or everted edge, often in an older patient and HPV-related, sometimes with hard inguinal nodes. Any persistent or atypical ulcer must be biopsied.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Why must every patient with a genital ulcer be tested for HIV?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Genital ulcers breach the mucosal barrier and increase both HIV transmission and acquisition; a painful ulcer with fever, rash and lymphadenopathy may itself be HIV seroconversion. Offer PEP after exposure and PrEP for prevention.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is a fixed drug eruption in the context of genital ulcers?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A well-demarcated lesion or ulcer that recurs at the same site each time a causative drug is taken; recognising the temporal drug relationship is key to diagnosis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is the first-line treatment for a first episode of genital herpes?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Oral aciclovir (or valaciclovir), with analgesia and saline bathing; severe cases with urinary retention may need catheterisation. Recurrences are usually milder and may be managed episodically or with suppressive therapy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Beyond specific treatment, what management steps apply to any sexually transmitted genital ulcer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A full STI screen (including HIV and syphilis), partner notification and contact tracing, safety-netting/abstinence advice, and consideration of safeguarding in the young or vulnerable.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is the commonest pathological genital lump, and how does it look?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Anogenital warts, caused by low-risk HPV (types 6 and 11). They are soft, fleshy, painless, cauliflower-like or filiform papules and may be multiple.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: How is molluscum contagiosum distinguished from genital warts?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Molluscum are pearly, dome-shaped, umbilicated papules with a central dimple (caused by a poxvirus), whereas warts are rough, fleshy and cauliflower-like. Both are usually painless.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What are condylomata lata and why must they not be mistaken for ordinary warts?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Broad, flat, moist warty plaques of secondary syphilis, occurring in warm moist folds. They are highly infectious and reflect systemic disease, so syphilis serology is required (treatment is penicillin, not wart therapy).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Which features of a genital lump should prompt an urgent biopsy?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A solitary, hard, ulcerated, bleeding or non-healing lump, or a pigmented/irregular/changing lesion — suggesting penile or vulval carcinoma or melanoma. Do not freeze or treat blindly.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Name three benign 'normal variant' genital lumps that commonly worry patients.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Pearly penile papules (regular rows around the corona), Fordyce spots (ectopic sebaceous glands), and vestibular papillomatosis in women. All are normal and need only reassurance.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What is a Bartholin's cyst/abscess and how is an abscess managed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A cyst/abscess of the Bartholin's gland presenting as a unilateral swelling at the posterior labia (around 4 or 8 o'clock). An abscess is tense and painful and is managed with incision and drainage or marsupialisation (with antibiotics if needed).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: When should florid warts or molluscum prompt further concern?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: When they are unusually florid, extensive or atypical in an adult, consider underlying immunosuppression, particularly HIV, and test accordingly.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What are the first-line treatments for anogenital warts?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Topical agents (podophyllotoxin or imiquimod) or ablative/physical methods (cryotherapy, electrocautery). Many resolve spontaneously; HPV vaccination helps prevent them.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Why is safeguarding relevant when a child presents with anogenital warts?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Anogenital warts in a child may raise the possibility of sexual abuse and warrant safeguarding assessment, although vertical (perinatal) and non-sexual transmission also occur; a careful, non-judgemental evaluation is needed.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What accompanying features would support a diagnosis of secondary syphilis in a patient with genital plaques?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A widespread rash including the palms and soles, mucous patches, generalised lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, alongside the moist condylomata lata; confirm with treponemal serology.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: What are scabetic nodules and where do they occur?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: Persistent itchy inflammatory nodules of scabies, characteristically on the penis and scrotum (and other sites), often with burrows elsewhere; the itch is typically worse at night.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.front: Beyond specific treatment, what general steps apply to sexually transmitted genital lumps?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.back: A full STI screen (including HIV and syphilis), partner notification where relevant, HPV vaccination and cervical/anal screening advice, and reassurance for normal variants.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: What is the single key question when examining a discrete testicular lump?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Is it arising from the testis, or separate from it? A solid lump arising from the testis is testicular cancer until proven otherwise; a lump clearly separate from the testis is almost always benign.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: A young man finds a painless, solid, hard lump within the body of the testis that does not transilluminate. What must you assume and do?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Testicular cancer until proven otherwise. Arrange urgent scrotal ultrasound and tumour markers (AFP, β-hCG, LDH) and refer to urology; never reassure without imaging.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: Which age group is most affected by testicular germ-cell tumours?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Men aged roughly 15–35 years; testicular cancer is the commonest solid malignancy in this group and is highly curable when detected early.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: Which tumour markers are used in suspected testicular cancer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: AFP, beta-hCG and LDH — used for diagnosis, staging and monitoring of germ-cell tumours.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: How does an epididymal cyst present, and how is it distinguished from a tumour?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: As a painless lump that is separate from the testis (above and behind it) and transilluminates. Unlike a tumour, it does not arise from the testis and is fluid-filled on ultrasound.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: What is a varicocele and what is a key associated concern?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: A 'bag of worms' of dilated pampiniform veins above the testis, usually left-sided and decompressing on lying flat, sometimes causing ache or subfertility. A new, right-sided or non-decompressing varicocele warrants renal imaging to exclude a renal mass.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: A patient has a tender testicular/epididymal lump with fever and dysuria, relieved by elevating the testis. What is the likely diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Epididymo-orchitis (STI-related in young men, coliform/UTI in older men). If there is any doubt about torsion, the patient should be explored.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: Why must a firm testis be imaged even when there is a surrounding hydrocele?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: A reactive (secondary) hydrocele can form around an underlying testicular tumour; a firm or irregular testis needs ultrasound to avoid missing a cancer hidden by the fluid.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: What is the definitive surgical procedure for a confirmed testicular tumour, and what should precede it?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Radical inguinal orchidectomy (with oncology input for further treatment). Sperm banking should be offered beforehand, as treatment may affect fertility.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: Why is testicular self-examination important, and what should be taught?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Because early detection of testicular cancer greatly improves the already high cure rate. Men should regularly feel each testis, noting any new lump, change in size or firmness, and seek review promptly.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: A sudden, painful testicular swelling with a high-riding testis and absent cremasteric reflex is found. What is the diagnosis and the correct action?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: Testicular torsion — a surgical emergency requiring immediate scrotal exploration (within about 6 hours); do not delay for imaging.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.front: How does 'testicular lump' differ in emphasis from 'scrotal swelling' as presentations?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.back: A testicular lump is a discrete palpable nodule (often self-detected), focusing on whether it is intratesticular (cancer) or separate (benign). Scrotal swelling refers to the whole hemiscrotum enlarging (fluid, hernia, generalised causes), which is worked up by the 'can you get above it / transilluminate' approach.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: Why is new-onset erectile dysfunction clinically important beyond sexual health?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: It is an early, independent marker of cardiovascular disease — the smaller penile arteries narrow before the coronaries, so ED can precede angina or myocardial infarction by years. Every man with ED should have his cardiovascular and metabolic risk assessed.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: How does the history distinguish organic from psychogenic erectile dysfunction?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Organic ED is gradual and global with loss of early-morning/nocturnal erections. Psychogenic ED is sudden and situational with preserved nocturnal/early-morning erections and a clear stressor or relationship context.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: What is the significance of preserved early-morning erections in a man with ED?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Their preservation points to a psychogenic cause (the physiological erectile mechanism is intact), whereas their loss suggests an organic cause (vascular, neurogenic or endocrine).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: List the main categories of organic erectile dysfunction.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Vascular (commonest), neurogenic, endocrine, and drug-induced. Anatomical causes such as Peyronie's disease also contribute.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: Which endocrine abnormalities should be screened for in ED, and how?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Hypogonadism (a morning testosterone, repeated with LH/FSH if low), hyperprolactinaemia (prolactin, then pituitary MRI), and thyroid disease (TFTs). Low libido and fatigue point to hypogonadism; galactorrhoea or visual-field loss to a prolactinoma.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: Name common drug classes that cause erectile dysfunction.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Antihypertensives (thiazides, beta-blockers), antidepressants (SSRIs), 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors (finasteride), antipsychotics, and opioids; alcohol and smoking also contribute. A medication review is part of every ED assessment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: Which investigations form the baseline work-up for erectile dysfunction?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: HbA1c or fasting glucose, a lipid profile, and a morning testosterone, with prolactin and TFTs where indicated, plus an overall cardiovascular risk assessment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: What is first-line drug treatment for ED, and what is the key contraindication?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: A phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitor such as sildenafil or tadalafil. It is contraindicated with nitrates (and caution with alpha-blockers) because of the risk of severe hypotension.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: How do neurogenic causes of ED typically present, and give examples.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: With associated neurological features (sensory changes, bladder/bowel symptoms). Examples include diabetic neuropathy, multiple sclerosis, spinal cord disorders, and pelvic nerve damage from radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: What lifestyle and risk-factor measures help erectile dysfunction?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Stopping smoking, losing weight, regular exercise, reducing alcohol, and optimising blood pressure, lipids and glucose — these both improve erectile function and reduce cardiovascular risk.
A fibrous plaque of the tunica albuginea causing penile curvature and sometimes painful erections or ED; a palpable plaque is felt on the shaft.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.front: Why is ED often described as a presenting feature of diabetes?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.back: Diabetes causes both vascular and neuropathic damage impairing erections, and ED frequently develops before diabetes is formally diagnosed, so checking HbA1c/glucose is essential.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: What is the overall approach to a man presenting with haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Stratify by age and red flags. Under 40 with a single/few episodes and no red flags is almost always benign and self-limiting (reassure after examination and urinalysis). Over 40, persistent/recurrent, or with red flags requires investigation to exclude prostate and genitourinary malignancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: Which features are 'red flags' that change haematospermia from benign to needing work-up?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Age over 40, persistent or recurrent episodes, visible haematuria, abnormal prostate on DRE, lower urinary tract symptoms, weight loss, and an abnormal genital examination.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: What is the commonest identifiable cause of haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Infection or inflammation of the prostate/seminal tract — prostatitis, seminal vesiculitis, epididymo-orchitis or urethritis (including STIs).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: How should haematospermia accompanied by visible haematuria be managed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Via the haematuria pathway — investigate for bladder and upper-tract malignancy with cystoscopy and CT urogram, rather than attributing it to a benign cause.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: Which investigations are appropriate in an older man or one with persistent haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Digital rectal examination and PSA (with informed discussion), urine dip and culture, an STI screen, clotting/INR and blood pressure, and MRI of the prostate/seminal vesicles with urology referral if persistent or red flags are present.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: Which systemic and drug causes of haematospermia should be considered?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Bleeding disorders and anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs), and uncontrolled hypertension. Check clotting/INR and blood pressure.
Recent prostate biopsy, vasectomy, urethral instrumentation and perineal trauma; these are usually self-limiting and settle over a few weeks.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: When should genitourinary tuberculosis or schistosomiasis be considered as a cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: In men with relevant travel/residence in endemic areas and chronic or persistent symptoms; these can involve the seminal vesicles and genitourinary tract.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: What examination should every man with haematospermia have?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: A digital rectal examination of the prostate (size, texture, tenderness), examination of the external genitalia/epididymis, a blood-pressure check, and urinalysis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: What reassurance can be given to a young man with a single episode of haematospermia and normal findings?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: That it is very likely benign, idiopathic and self-limiting; he should be safety-netted to return if it persists, recurs, or is accompanied by haematuria, pain or other red-flag features.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: Why is a PSA useful in the assessment of haematospermia in older men?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Because persistent haematospermia in men over 40 can rarely be a presenting feature of prostate cancer; PSA (with DRE and, if indicated, MRI/biopsy) helps exclude it.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.front: Which STIs and infections should prompt targeted treatment in haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.back: Prostatitis and seminal vesiculitis (bacterial), and sexually transmitted urethritis such as chlamydia and gonorrhoea; treat with appropriate antibiotics and offer partner management.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: What is the first and most useful way to classify dyspareunia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: By site: superficial (entry/introital) pain versus deep (pelvic) pain. This immediately narrows the differential and directs examination.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: List the main causes of superficial dyspareunia.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Vulvovaginal infection (candida, herpes), atrophic vaginitis of the menopause, vulval dermatoses (lichen sclerosus/planus), vaginismus, vulvodynia, and inadequate lubrication.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: List the main causes of deep dyspareunia.
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Endometriosis/adenomyosis, pelvic inflammatory disease, uterine fibroids, ovarian pathology, pelvic adhesions, and (as a red flag) gynaecological malignancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: Which red-flag features of deep dyspareunia should prompt exclusion of gynaecological cancer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: A pelvic mass, post-coital or intermenstrual bleeding, postmenopausal bleeding, and weight loss. Examine, image, and biopsy/colposcope a suspicious cervix.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: How does endometriosis typically present with dyspareunia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Deep, often cyclical dyspareunia with dysmenorrhoea, chronic pelvic pain and subfertility; examination may reveal uterosacral nodularity or a fixed, retroverted uterus. Laparoscopy is the gold-standard diagnostic test.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: What is atrophic vaginitis and how is it treated?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Genitourinary syndrome of the menopause: superficial dyspareunia with vaginal dryness, burning and spotting due to low oestrogen. It responds well to topical (vaginal) oestrogen and lubricants.

Involuntary spasm of the pelvic-floor muscles on attempted penetration, often with anticipatory anxiety and sometimes past trauma; it causes superficial dyspareunia and is managed with education, pelvic-floor physiotherapy and psychosexual therapy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: Which vulval dermatoses cause superficial dyspareunia and how do they look?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Lichen sclerosus (white, atrophic, 'figure-of-eight' perineal skin, fissuring) and lichen planus (erosive vulval change). They are treated with potent topical steroids and need monitoring, as lichen sclerosus carries a small vulval cancer risk.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: How does PID present with deep dyspareunia and how should it be managed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Deep dyspareunia with vaginal discharge, fever and cervical motion tenderness; it is treated empirically with antibiotics to protect fertility, alongside STI screening and partner notification.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: Which examination is essential to evaluate deep dyspareunia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: A bimanual pelvic examination (with speculum) assessing for uterine/adnexal tenderness, masses, cervical excitation and uterosacral nodularity, alongside vulval inspection.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: What investigations are appropriate for dyspareunia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Vaginal/endocervical swabs and STI screen with vaginal pH, pelvic ultrasound for masses/endometriosis, cervical smear/colposcopy for a suspicious cervix, and laparoscopy where endometriosis is suspected.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.front: Why is a sensitive psychosexual and trauma history important in dyspareunia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.back: Because psychosexual factors, relationship issues and past sexual trauma may underlie or contribute to the pain (especially vaginismus and vulvodynia), and safeguarding concerns may need addressing.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: How should anogenital itch or rash be classified?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Into infective, inflammatory, or neoplastic causes. Most cases are inflammatory (irritant/contact dermatitis being commonest); the key is not to miss lichen sclerosus and neoplasia.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: Which anogenital lesions must be biopsied rather than re-treated?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Any persistent, thickened, ulcerated, pigmented or steroid-unresponsive lesion — it may be vulval/anal intraepithelial neoplasia, squamous cell carcinoma, extramammary Paget's disease or melanoma.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: What are the features of lichen sclerosus and why does it matter?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Itchy, white, atrophic skin in a 'figure-of-eight' distribution with fissuring and scarring (fusion/phimosis). It needs a potent topical steroid and monitoring because of a small risk of vulval (or penile) carcinoma.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: What is the commonest cause of an anogenital rash, and how is it managed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Irritant/contact dermatitis (soaps, wipes, moisture, over-washing). Management is removing the irritant, using an emollient/soap substitute, and a short course of topical steroid.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: How does candidal anogenital infection typically appear?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Itch with erythema and characteristic satellite red papules/pustules, often with a cottage-cheese vaginal discharge; commoner in diabetes, pregnancy and after antibiotics.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: How is tinea cruris recognised and confirmed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: A well-demarcated, annular groin rash with central clearing and an active scaly edge; confirm with skin scrapings for dermatophyte and treat with a topical (or oral) antifungal.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: A child has intense nocturnal perianal itch. What is the likely cause and management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Threadworm (Enterobius vermicularis). Diagnose clinically or with a perianal tape test, and treat the child and household with an anti-helminthic (e.g. mebendazole) plus hygiene measures.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: What features suggest scabies as a cause of anogenital itch?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Generalised itch worse at night with burrows (e.g. in the finger webs) and inflammatory papules/nodules on the penis and scrotum; treat with topical permethrin and treat close contacts.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: Which systemic conditions can cause generalised pruritus that includes the anogenital area?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: Diabetes (recurrent candida), iron deficiency, cholestasis, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease and lymphoma. Investigate with FBC, ferritin, glucose/HbA1c, LFTs, U&E and TFTs.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: How does inverse (flexural) psoriasis differ from psoriasis elsewhere?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: It appears as well-demarcated, salmon-pink plaques in the flexures/genital folds with minimal scale (because of moisture), rather than the thick silvery scale seen at typical sites.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: What perpetuates chronic anogenital itch even after the initial cause resolves?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: The itch-scratch cycle and over-washing/over-treatment, which can produce lichen simplex chronicus; breaking the cycle with emollients and stopping irritants is essential.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.front: What is extramammary Paget's disease of the anogenital skin?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.back: An intraepithelial adenocarcinoma presenting as a well-demarcated, eczema-like plaque that characteristically fails to respond to topical steroids; a persistent 'eczema' that won't clear should be biopsied.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A 24-year-old man has a profuse, purulent urethral discharge and dysuria for 2 days. What is the most likely diagnosis and the essential test?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Profuse purulent urethral discharge suggests gonorrhoea; NAAT confirms it but culture is essential to detect antibiotic resistance.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A 30-year-old woman has thin, grey, fishy-smelling discharge with a vaginal pH of 5.0 and clue cells on microscopy. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Thin grey fishy discharge with pH >4.5 and clue cells fulfils the Amsel criteria for bacterial vaginosis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A 22-year-old woman has deep pelvic pain, fever, and cervical motion tenderness with a mucopurulent cervix. What is the most appropriate management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: This is pelvic inflammatory disease; empirical antibiotics are started at once because delay risks tubal damage, infertility and ectopic pregnancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A woman has thick white 'cottage-cheese' discharge with vulval itch and no odour. Which additional factor most predisposes to this condition?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: This is candidiasis; recent antibiotics (as well as diabetes and pregnancy) predispose to it. It is not sexually transmitted.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: Which discharge feature is most suggestive of trichomoniasis?
options: Frothy yellow-green with a strawberry cervix
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: A frothy yellow-green offensive discharge with a strawberry cervix is characteristic of Trichomonas vaginalis, a sexually transmitted protozoan.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A 26-year-old man has a scant mucoid urethral discharge with mild dysuria; NAAT is positive for chlamydia. What is the first-line treatment?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Chlamydial (non-gonococcal) urethritis is treated first-line with doxycycline.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: Which single measure is essential in the management of every sexually transmitted cause of discharge?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Partner notification (and screening/treatment) prevents reinfection and onward transmission and is core to STI management.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A pregnant woman presents with vaginal discharge and lower abdominal pain. Which diagnosis must be actively excluded first?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: In a pregnant woman with pain, an ectopic pregnancy must be excluded before attributing symptoms to a benign discharge.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: What is the recommended specimen for gonorrhoea and chlamydia NAAT in a man versus a woman?
options: First-pass urine in men, vulvovaginal swab in women
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: First-pass (first-catch) urine is optimal in men and a vulvovaginal swab in women for chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: Which of the following is NOT a sexually transmitted cause of vaginal discharge?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Bacterial vaginosis results from anaerobic overgrowth and is not classed as a sexually transmitted infection, unlike trichomoniasis, chlamydia, gonorrhoea and herpes.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A patient with gonorrhoea develops migratory joint pains, tenosynovitis and a pustular rash. What does this represent?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: Disseminated gonococcal infection can cause the triad of migratory arthritis/tenosynovitis and a pustular rash.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.question: A woman reports an offensive vaginal discharge; on speculum examination a forgotten tampon is found. What is the appropriate action?
options: Prescribe metronidazole and discharge without examination
Remove the foreign body and treat any secondary infection
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ur.explanation: A retained foreign body should be removed and any secondary infection treated; it is a readily reversible cause of offensive discharge.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 25-year-old has multiple painful shallow genital ulcers preceded by vesicles, with tender inguinal nodes and dysuria. What is the most likely diagnosis and confirmatory test?
options: Genital herpes; HSV PCR of the lesion
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Painful, multiple, vesicle-preceded ulcers with tender nodes are typical of genital herpes; HSV PCR of a lesion swab confirms it.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 30-year-old has a single painless, indurated genital ulcer with a clean base and non-tender rubbery inguinal nodes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A painless, solitary, indurated 'clean' ulcer (chancre) with rubbery nodes is characteristic of primary syphilis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which investigation best confirms primary syphilis at the ulcer stage?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Dark-ground microscopy of the chancre plus treponemal serology confirms primary syphilis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 70-year-old man has a chronic, indurated, non-healing penile ulcer with a rolled edge and a hard inguinal node. What is the essential next step?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A chronic indurated non-healing ulcer with a rolled edge is penile carcinoma until proven otherwise; biopsy is essential before any empirical treatment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which single test should be offered to EVERY patient presenting with a genital ulcer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: All genital ulcers increase HIV transmission/acquisition and may represent seroconversion, so an HIV test (with a full STI screen) is offered to everyone.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A young adult has recurrent painful oral and genital ulcers, an inflamed eye and a positive pathergy test. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Recurrent oral and genital ulcers with uveitis and a positive pathergy test indicate Behcet's disease.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A traveller returns with a painful, ragged, undermined genital ulcer and a fluctuant, suppurative inguinal bubo. Which organism is most likely?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A painful ragged undermined ulcer with suppurative inguinal buboes is chancroid, caused by Haemophilus ducreyi.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A patient reports a genital ulcer that appears at exactly the same site each time they take a particular medication. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A lesion recurring at the same site with a specific drug is a fixed drug eruption; the temporal drug relationship is diagnostic.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: What is the first-line antimicrobial treatment for confirmed primary syphilis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Primary syphilis is treated with intramuscular benzathine penicillin (with partner notification and screening).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A patient presents 3 weeks after a high-risk exposure with a painful genital ulcer, fever, a maculopapular rash and generalised lymphadenopathy. What must be considered?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A genital ulcer with fever, rash and lymphadenopathy after exposure may represent HIV seroconversion; test for HIV and screen fully.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which combination best fits secondary syphilis?
options: Painful vesicles on the penis only
A widespread rash including palms and soles with mucous patches and condylomata lata
A single painless indurated ulcer only
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Secondary syphilis features a widespread rash (classically involving palms and soles), mucous patches and condylomata lata, reflecting dissemination after the primary chancre.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A first episode of genital herpes causes severe pain and acute urinary retention. Alongside aciclovir, what supportive step may be required?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Severe first-episode herpes can cause urinary retention; catheterisation may be needed alongside aciclovir, analgesia and saline bathing.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 22-year-old has several soft, painless, cauliflower-like lumps on the penis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Soft, fleshy, cauliflower-like painless papules are anogenital warts caused by low-risk HPV (6/11).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A patient has pearly, dome-shaped papules with a central umbilication. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Pearly, umbilicated papules with a central dimple are molluscum contagiosum, caused by a poxvirus.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A patient has broad, flat, moist warty plaques in the perineal folds and a rash on the palms and soles. What is the diagnosis and key test?
options: Condylomata lata of secondary syphilis; treponemal serology
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Flat moist plaques (condylomata lata) with a palm/sole rash indicate secondary syphilis; confirm with treponemal serology and treat with penicillin.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 68-year-old man has a solitary, hard, non-healing ulcerated lump on the glans with a firm inguinal node. What is the essential next step?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A solitary, hard, non-healing lump with lymphadenopathy is penile carcinoma until proven otherwise; biopsy is essential before any treatment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A man is worried about small dome-shaped papules arranged in regular rows around the corona of the glans. They are asymptomatic. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Regular rows of small papules around the corona are pearly penile papules — a normal variant requiring only reassurance.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A woman presents with a tense, painful unilateral swelling at the posterior aspect of the labia. What is the most appropriate management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A tense painful posterior-labial swelling is a Bartholin's abscess, managed with incision and drainage or marsupialisation.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which underlying condition should be considered when genital warts or molluscum are unusually florid in an adult?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Florid or atypical warts/molluscum in an adult should prompt testing for HIV and other causes of immunosuppression.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which is a recognised first-line treatment for anogenital warts?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Anogenital warts are treated with topical agents such as imiquimod or podophyllotoxin, or with ablative methods like cryotherapy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A 5-year-old girl is found to have anogenital warts. What is the most appropriate response?
options: Immediately assume abuse and inform police
Undertake a careful safeguarding assessment while recognising other transmission routes
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Anogenital warts in a child warrant a careful, non-judgemental safeguarding assessment, bearing in mind that vertical and non-sexual transmission also occur.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which lump is a benign cyst that may become a painful abscess and, if recurrent in older women, may warrant biopsy to exclude carcinoma?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: A Bartholin's cyst can become a painful abscess; recurrence in older women warrants biopsy to exclude carcinoma of the gland.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: Which feature most reliably separates condylomata lata from anogenital (HPV) warts?
options: They are flat, moist plaques with positive syphilis serology
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Condylomata lata are flat, moist plaques of secondary syphilis with positive treponemal serology, unlike the cauliflower-like HPV warts.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.question: A patient has itchy nodules on the penis and scrotum with burrows in the finger webs, worse at night. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ge.explanation: Itchy genital nodules with burrows and nocturnal itch indicate scabies (scabetic nodules).

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A 28-year-old man finds a painless, hard lump arising from the body of the right testis; it does not transilluminate. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Urgent scrotal ultrasound and tumour markers
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: A solid, painless intratesticular lump is testicular cancer until proven otherwise; urgent scrotal ultrasound with tumour markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) is required.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: Which feature best distinguishes a benign epididymal cyst from a testicular tumour?
options: It is separate from the testis and transilluminates
It is associated with weight loss
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: An epididymal cyst lies separate from the testis (above and behind) and transilluminates, unlike a solid tumour arising from the testis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: Which tumour markers are most useful in a suspected testicular germ-cell tumour?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: AFP, beta-hCG and LDH are the key markers for testicular germ-cell tumours.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A 30-year-old man has a new right-sided 'bag of worms' that does not decompress on lying flat. What should you do?
options: Image the kidneys to exclude a renal mass
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: A new, right-sided or non-decompressing varicocele may reflect a renal mass obstructing venous drainage; image the kidneys.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A 24-year-old has a tender swelling of the epididymis with fever and dysuria, eased by elevation. What is the most likely diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: A tender epididymis with fever, dysuria and relief on elevation suggests epididymo-orchitis; torsion must still be excluded if there is doubt.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: Which is the single most important investigation for any solid or uncertain testicular lump?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: Scrotal ultrasound (with Doppler) is the key first-line investigation for a solid or uncertain testicular lump.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A firm, irregular testis is found with a surrounding hydrocele. What is the correct interpretation?
options: The testis must be imaged to exclude an underlying tumour
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: A reactive hydrocele can conceal a testicular tumour; a firm, irregular testis must be imaged with ultrasound.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: What should be offered to a young man before orchidectomy for a testicular tumour?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: Sperm banking should be offered before orchidectomy and oncological treatment, which may impair fertility.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A 17-year-old presents with a sudden, painful testicular swelling; the testis is high-riding and the cremasteric reflex is absent. What is the correct management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: This is testicular torsion, a surgical emergency requiring immediate exploration within about 6 hours; do not delay for imaging.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: Which statement about testicular cancer is correct?
options: It is the commonest solid cancer in young men and highly curable when caught early
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: Testicular cancer is the commonest solid malignancy in men aged 15–35 and has an excellent cure rate, especially with early detection.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: A man reports a 'lump' that, on examination, is clearly the normal epididymis, with a normal testis and no other features. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Reassurance after careful examination (and self-exam education)
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: When the 'lump' is the normal epididymis and the testis is normal, reassurance and education about self-examination are appropriate.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.question: Which factor is a recognised risk factor for testicular cancer?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Te.explanation: A history of undescended testis (cryptorchidism) increases the risk of testicular cancer, as does a positive family history.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A 55-year-old man reports gradual, progressive erectile dysfunction over 2 years with loss of morning erections. He smokes and has hypertension. What does this presentation most strongly suggest?
options: Vasculogenic ED and increased cardiovascular risk
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Gradual, global ED with loss of morning erections in a man with vascular risk factors is vasculogenic; it also flags increased cardiovascular risk warranting assessment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A 30-year-old man has sudden-onset ED that occurs only with his partner; his early-morning erections are normal. What is the most likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Sudden, situational ED with preserved morning erections indicates a psychogenic cause.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: Which single question is most useful in separating organic from psychogenic ED?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Preserved early-morning/nocturnal erections indicate a psychogenic cause; their loss indicates an organic one.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A man with ED also reports low libido, fatigue, and small testes. Which investigation is most appropriate?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: These features suggest hypogonadism; a morning serum testosterone (repeated with LH/FSH if low) is the appropriate test.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A man with ED reports galactorrhoea and has a bitemporal visual-field defect. What is the likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Galactorrhoea with a bitemporal field defect suggests a prolactinoma causing hyperprolactinaemia; check prolactin and arrange pituitary MRI.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: Which medication is a recognised cause of erectile dysfunction?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Thiazide diuretics and beta-blockers are well-recognised causes of drug-induced ED; a medication review is important.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A 60-year-old develops ED after radical prostatectomy. What is the mechanism?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: Radical prostatectomy can damage the cavernous nerves, producing a neurogenic ED.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: Which is the most appropriate first-line pharmacological treatment for ED once the cause is addressed?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: A PDE5 inhibitor is first-line drug treatment; testosterone is reserved for confirmed hypogonadism.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A man taking regular nitrates for angina requests treatment for ED. Why must a PDE5 inhibitor be avoided?
options: The combination with nitrates can cause severe hypotension
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: PDE5 inhibitors are contraindicated with nitrates because the combination can precipitate severe, dangerous hypotension.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: What is the most appropriate baseline blood panel for a man presenting with erectile dysfunction?
options: HbA1c, lipids and a morning testosterone
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: HbA1c/glucose, lipids and a morning testosterone (with prolactin/TFTs if indicated) form the baseline work-up, alongside cardiovascular risk assessment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: A man with ED reports intermittent claudication and exertional chest tightness. What does the ED most likely represent here?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: With claudication and exertional chest symptoms, the ED is part of systemic atherosclerotic disease and mandates cardiovascular assessment.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.question: Which finding on genital examination would specifically suggest Peyronie's disease?
options: A palpable fibrous plaque with penile curvature
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Er.explanation: A palpable fibrous plaque on the shaft with penile curvature is characteristic of Peyronie's disease.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A 28-year-old man reports a single episode of blood in his semen. He has no urinary symptoms, a normal examination and clear urine. What is the most appropriate management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: A young man with an isolated episode, no red flags and normal findings has benign idiopathic haematospermia; reassurance and safety-netting are appropriate.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A 62-year-old man has recurrent haematospermia over several months, mild LUTS, and a hard nodule on the prostate. What is the most important next step?
options: PSA and referral for prostate MRI/biopsy
Repeat semen analysis in a year
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Persistent haematospermia in a man over 40 with an abnormal DRE requires PSA and referral for prostate MRI/biopsy to exclude prostate cancer.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A 40-year-old man has haematospermia together with visible haematuria. Which pathway should he follow?
options: The haematuria pathway (cystoscopy and CT urogram)
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Haematospermia with visible haematuria warrants the haematuria pathway to exclude bladder and upper-tract malignancy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A 30-year-old man has haematospermia with dysuria, frequency and a tender prostate. What is the most likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Dysuria, frequency and a tender prostate suggest prostatitis/seminal vesiculitis, the commonest identifiable cause; screen for infection and STIs.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A man on warfarin presents with haematospermia. Which investigation is most relevant to his medication?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Anticoagulation can cause haematospermia; checking the INR/clotting is directly relevant.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: Which of the following is a recognised iatrogenic cause of haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Recent prostate biopsy (and vasectomy or instrumentation) commonly causes transient, self-limiting haematospermia.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A returning traveller from an endemic region has chronic haematospermia. Which infections should be considered?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: In relevant travellers with chronic symptoms, genitourinary tuberculosis and schistosomiasis should be considered.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: Which single examination is essential in the assessment of haematospermia, especially in older men?
options: Digital rectal examination of the prostate
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: A digital rectal examination assesses the prostate for size, texture and tenderness and is essential, particularly in older men.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: A 45-year-old man has persistent haematospermia despite a normal DRE and normal PSA. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
options: MRI of the prostate/seminal vesicles with urology referral
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Persistent haematospermia, even with a normal DRE and PSA, warrants MRI of the prostate/seminal vesicles and urological referral.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: Which systemic condition, if uncontrolled, is a recognised cause of haematospermia?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Uncontrolled hypertension is a recognised systemic cause; blood pressure should be checked and managed.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: What is the key safety-netting advice for a young man reassured about benign haematospermia?
options: Return if it persists, recurs, or is associated with haematuria or pain
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: He should return if symptoms persist or recur, or if haematuria, pain or other red-flag features develop.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.question: In a man under 40 with haematospermia, which factor would most prompt further investigation rather than simple reassurance?
options: Persistent or recurrent episodes with red flags
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Ha.explanation: Persistent or recurrent haematospermia with red flags warrants investigation even in younger men, whereas an isolated episode with normal findings can be reassured.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A 52-year-old postmenopausal woman reports superficial pain on penetration with vaginal dryness and occasional spotting. What is the most likely diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Superficial dyspareunia with dryness and spotting after the menopause is atrophic vaginitis (genitourinary syndrome of the menopause), treated with topical oestrogen — but any postmenopausal bleeding still requires exclusion of endometrial cancer (transvaginal ultrasound ± biopsy) before attributing it to atrophy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A 30-year-old woman has deep, cyclical dyspareunia with severe dysmenorrhoea and difficulty conceiving. Examination shows uterosacral nodularity. What is the most likely diagnosis and gold-standard test?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Cyclical deep dyspareunia with dysmenorrhoea, subfertility and uterosacral nodularity indicates endometriosis; laparoscopy is the gold-standard diagnostic test.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A 26-year-old has deep dyspareunia with purulent vaginal discharge, fever, and cervical motion tenderness. What is the most appropriate management?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: This is pelvic inflammatory disease; empirical antibiotics are started to protect fertility, with STI screening and partner notification.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A 60-year-old woman has new deep dyspareunia, a pelvic mass and postmenopausal bleeding. What is the priority?
options: Urgent assessment to exclude gynaecological malignancy
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Deep dyspareunia with a pelvic mass and postmenopausal bleeding is a red flag for gynaecological cancer and requires urgent examination, imaging and biopsy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A young woman experiences involuntary tightening that prevents penetration, with marked anticipatory anxiety and a normal examination when relaxed. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Involuntary pelvic-floor muscle spasm on attempted penetration with anticipatory anxiety and no organic lesion is vaginismus.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A woman has superficial dyspareunia with vulval itch and a thick, white, cottage-cheese discharge. What is the likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Itch with a thick white cottage-cheese discharge indicates vulvovaginal candidiasis causing superficial dyspareunia.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A woman has superficial dyspareunia with white, atrophic 'figure-of-eight' perineal skin and fissuring. What is the diagnosis and a key long-term concern?
options: Lichen sclerosus; small risk of vulval carcinoma
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: White atrophic figure-of-eight vulval skin with fissuring is lichen sclerosus; it is treated with potent topical steroids and monitored because of a small vulval cancer risk.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: Which examination finding most specifically supports a diagnosis of endometriosis in a woman with deep dyspareunia?
options: Uterosacral nodularity / a fixed retroverted uterus
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Uterosacral nodularity and a fixed, retroverted uterus support endometriosis, which is confirmed at laparoscopy.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: Which investigation is most appropriate to assess deep dyspareunia with a suspected pelvic mass?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Pelvic ultrasound is the appropriate first-line imaging to assess a suspected pelvic mass or endometrioma in deep dyspareunia.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: What is the first-line treatment for superficial dyspareunia due to atrophic vaginitis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Atrophic vaginitis responds to topical vaginal oestrogen and lubricants, restoring vaginal epithelial health.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: Which management is most appropriate for vaginismus and vulvodynia?
options: Education, pelvic-floor physiotherapy and psychosexual therapy
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Vaginismus and vulvodynia are managed with education, pelvic-floor physiotherapy and psychosexual therapy rather than surgery.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.question: A woman with deep dyspareunia also reports heavy menstrual bleeding and has a bulky, tender uterus. What is the most likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__Dy.explanation: Deep dyspareunia with menorrhagia and a bulky, tender uterus suggests fibroids or adenomyosis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A 65-year-old woman has a persistent vulval plaque that has not responded to 3 months of topical steroid. What is the most appropriate next step?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: A persistent, steroid-unresponsive anogenital lesion must be biopsied to exclude VIN, squamous cell carcinoma or extramammary Paget's disease.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A woman has itchy, white, atrophic vulval skin in a figure-of-eight pattern with fissuring. What is the diagnosis and treatment?
options: Lichen sclerosus; potent topical steroid with monitoring
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: White atrophic figure-of-eight vulval skin with fissuring is lichen sclerosus, treated with a potent topical steroid and monitored for vulval carcinoma.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A 5-year-old boy has intense perianal itch that is worst at night. What is the most likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Intense nocturnal perianal itch in a child is characteristic of threadworm; treat the child and household with an anti-helminthic and hygiene measures.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A woman has vulval itch with erythema and satellite red papules, plus a thick white discharge. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Itch with satellite lesions and a cottage-cheese discharge indicates candidiasis.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A man develops a symmetrical, itchy genital rash a few days after using a new shower gel. What is the most likely cause?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: A symmetrical itchy rash after a new product suggests irritant/contact dermatitis; remove the irritant and use an emollient and short-term steroid.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A patient has a well-demarcated, annular groin rash with central clearing and a scaly active edge. What is the diagnosis?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: An annular rash with central clearing and a scaly edge is tinea cruris; confirm with scrapings and treat with an antifungal.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A patient has generalised itch worse at night with burrows in the finger webs and papules on the penis. What is the treatment?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: This is scabies; treat with topical permethrin and treat close contacts simultaneously.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A patient has generalised pruritus including the anogenital area, with weight loss and night sweats. Which investigation set is most appropriate?
options: FBC, ferritin, glucose/HbA1c, LFTs, U&E and TFTs
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Generalised pruritus with systemic features warrants a systemic screen (FBC, ferritin, glucose, LFTs, U&E, TFTs) to detect causes such as iron deficiency, cholestasis, renal disease or lymphoma.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: Which description best fits inverse (flexural) psoriasis of the genital area?
options: Well-demarcated salmon-pink plaques with minimal scale
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Inverse psoriasis appears as well-demarcated salmon-pink plaques with minimal scale in the moist flexures.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A persistent, eczema-like anogenital plaque repeatedly fails to respond to topical steroids. Which diagnosis must be excluded by biopsy?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: A steroid-unresponsive 'eczematous' plaque may be extramammary Paget's disease (an intraepithelial adenocarcinoma) and should be biopsied.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: Which single measure most helps break chronic idiopathic anogenital itch (pruritus ani/vulvae)?
options: Stopping irritants/over-washing and using emollients to break the itch-scratch cycle
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Stopping irritants and over-washing and using emollients breaks the itch-scratch cycle that perpetuates chronic pruritus.

signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.question: A woman with recurrent candidal vulvitis should be screened for which underlying condition?
signs__GENITOURINARY / SEXUAL HEALTH__An.explanation: Recurrent candidiasis should prompt screening for diabetes mellitus, which predisposes to candidal infection.
